lines: The City of Daly City receives federal entitlements in the form of Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) funds and HOME funds from the Department of Housing and Urban Development. These funds are integral to the City's efforts to help better the lives of low and moderate income persons in our community.

Each year, based on needs identified by the community, the City Council awards grants for public services, housing, and economic development activities with its CDBG funds. In order to be considered by the Council for funding, programs must address at least one of the following priority needs:
Increase the supply of affordable housing
Support public services that serve lower income persons and these groups: children and youth, the homeless, and special needs persons
Facilitate economic development by helping small businesses and entrepreneurs
The following organizations and their programs have been funded for PY 2026-27. Daly City residents can contact organizations directly to inquire about eligibility.
Daly City Partnership, After School Academic Programming - $20,000
HIP Housing, Housing Readiness for Seniors - $15,000
Legal Aid Society of San Mateo County, HomeSavers Project for Seniors and People with Disabilities (Eviction Prevention) - $25,000
Peninsula Family Service, Mission Child Development Center - $30,000
Project Read of North San Mateo County, Adult Literacy - $20,000
Rebuilding Together Peninsula, Safe At Home Minor Home Repair - $40,000
